The document editor (document.html) writes and edits text documents like Word or LibreOffice Writer: paragraphs and headings, fonts and colours, alignment and spacing, bullet and numbered lists, tables, images, headers and footers, find and replace. The editing component is Univer Docs.

Files

Format Open Save Notes
Word (.docx) yes yes page size and margins, styles, headings, text formatting, lists, tables, images, hyperlinks, headers and footers
OpenDocument (.odt, LibreOffice Writer) yes (also templates .ott) yes the same as for Word; footnotes and endnotes are placed at the end of the document
Word with macros (.docm), templates (.dotx) yes as .docx macros are not kept; a template becomes a new document
Text (.txt, .md) yes yes (.txt) only the text; formatting, tables and images are lost
Web page (.html) no yes text, formatting, lists, tables, images and links; no page layout
PDF no via 🖨 see Printing and PDF
  • Open (Ctrl+O) opens a file; you can also drop it onto the window. New starts an empty document.
  • Save (Ctrl+S) saves in the file's format: directly into the file in Chrome/Edge on the desktop, as a download in Firefox and on Android (replace the original file with it). Save as (Ctrl+Shift+S) asks for the name and the format.
  • The file name in the toolbar shows • while there are unsaved changes.

Printing and PDF

🖨 (Ctrl+P) prints the document with its page size and margins; choose Save as PDF (Chrome, Edge, Android) or Print to file (Firefox) as the printer to get a PDF. The header and footer of the document repeat on every page. The page breaks are made by the browser, so they can differ from the editor's pages; inserted page breaks are kept. Links stay clickable in the PDF, including the entries of a table of contents.

Documents from Word and LibreOffice are converted when they are opened; very complex layouts (text boxes, columns, tracked changes, comments) may look simpler. Keep the original file until you have checked the result. A "word" of more than 20,000 characters without a space (such as pasted base64 data) gets an invisible break point (U+200B) every 1,000 characters so that it can be shown; they are saved with the document.

Editing

The ribbon has the tabs Start (clipboard, bold/italic/underline/strike, sub- and superscript, paragraph style, size, font, colours, alignment, lists, checklists) and Insert (tables, images, page breaks, headers and footers). The usual shortcuts work: Ctrl+B/I/U, Ctrl+Z/Y, Ctrl+C/X/V, Ctrl+F to find. The status bar shows the word count and the zoom.

📐 Diagram in the toolbar opens an empty diagram in the diagram editor (a new window or tab); its first Save inserts the diagram as a picture at the cursor, later saves update it. When a diagram picture is selected (a click on it), 📐 Edit diagram opens it in the diagram editor again. An updated picture keeps its place and scale (at most the width of the text); Ctrl+Z undoes it. The diagram travels inside the picture (a PNG with the draw.io file), so it stays editable in the .docx file; Word shows the picture.

The language of the editing component follows the suite's language switch, and it follows the dark theme too.

Undo and redo are the first two buttons of the editor toolbar (also Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y).

Table of contents and footnotes

📑 Contents inserts a table of contents at the paragraph of the cursor: the headings (paragraph styles Heading 1 to Heading 5), indented by level. After changing headings, click it again to update the table in place. In saved Word and OpenDocument files the entries are links to the headings (Ctrl+click in Word, click in LibreOffice); the table has no page numbers (the editor does not know them) – Word and LibreOffice can add a real index with page numbers if needed.

Spelling

ABC✓ (F7) opens the spelling panel beside the document (below it on a phone). It lists the unknown words of the document text (headers and footers are not checked); words with digits, words in capitals (abbreviations), web and mail addresses are skipped.

  • Click a word to select it in the document; click again to go to its next occurrence. The panel shows suggestions: a suggestion replaces all occurrences of the word.
  • Ignore skips the word until the editor is closed; Add to dictionary keeps it in the browser for good (for all dictionaries).
  • ↻ Check again after editing the text.

English (US) and German (Germany) are built in. For other languages, Load dictionary… takes a Hunspell dictionary: either the .aff and the .dic file together (for example from a LibreOffice installation), or a LibreOffice dictionary extension (.oxt, for example from extensions.libreoffice.org). Loaded dictionaries stay in the browser and are chosen in the list; 🗑 removes the selected one. The dictionary, the added words and the ignored words are the same as in the ABC selector in the header and in the other applications (see Spelling in the user guide); the panel works whether that selector is on or off, because the page of this editor is drawn as an image and cannot show underlines.

Footnotes and endnotes of Word and LibreOffice files are shown with their number in superscript; their texts are placed at the end of the document after a line, because the editor has no footnote area. Page number fields in headers and footers show the number that was stored in the file.

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl. F1 (or ?) shows this list in the application.

On phones and tablets

Documents can be read and edited; the ribbon can be scrolled sideways. For longer texts a bigger screen and a keyboard are more comfortable.
